topic: Paediatric asthma: diagnosis, assessment and stepwise management

mcqs.question: How does the 2020 NAEPP update separate stepwise asthma care by age?

options.B: Fig 2 for ages 0–4, Fig 3 for ages 5–11, and Fig 4 for ages 12 and older
options.E: Age is ignored if spirometry is normal

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Fig 2 for ages 0–4, Fig 3 for ages 5–11, and Fig 4 for ages 12 and older
mcqs.explanation: The update states that each figure applies to one age group: 0–4, 5–11, and 12 years and older.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Fig 2 applies only to ages 0 to 4 years. Fig 3 applies only to ages 5 to 11 years. Fig 4 applies only to ages 12 years and older.

mcqs.question: What does the update call the currently preferred pharmacologic controller for persistent asthma?

options.B: Daily oral prednisolone for all ages
options.E: Long-term macrolide as the only controller

mcqs.explanation: The background text says scheduled daily ICS is the preferred controller for persistent asthma at all ages.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Scheduled, daily ICS treatment is the currently preferred pharmacologic controller therapy for persistent asthma in individuals of all ages.

mcqs.question: With which LABA does the NAEPP text say SMART has been used?

options.E: Any LABA is interchangeable in the cited SMART studies

mcqs.explanation: The update says this form of therapy has only been used with formoterol as the LABA.

sourceRefs.excerpt: This form of therapy has only been used with formoterol as the LABA.

mcqs.question: What maximum total daily formoterol dose does the update give for ages 4 to 11 years on SMART?
mcqs.explanation: The text caps formoterol at 8 puffs (36 μg) for ages 4 to 11 years and 12 puffs (54 μg) from age 12.

sourceRefs.excerpt: The maximum total daily dose of formoterol should not exceed 8 puffs (36 μg) for ages4 to11 years and12puffs (54 μg) for ages12 years and above.

mcqs.question: What does the update say clinicians use to choose the step of care?

options.B: Whether the child is newly diagnosed (treatment-naive) or already on treatment, within the age-specific figure
options.C: Adult GINA step 5 for every child

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Whether the child is newly diagnosed (treatment-naive) or already on treatment, within the age-specific figure
mcqs.explanation: Clinicians choose the step according to whether the individual is newly diagnosed or already treated, using the figure for that age.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Clinicians decide which step of care is appropriate depending on whether the individual is newly diagnosed
